01-neutral.name: ENSO-neutral equatorial Pacific
01-neutral.question: Under normal trade winds, where does warm surface water collect?
01-neutral.answerNote: Normal easterly trades push warm surface water westward; cooler water rises in the east.

02-el-nino.name: El Niño equatorial Pacific
02-el-nino.question: Compared with neutral conditions, what happens to the easterly trade winds?
02-el-nino.answerNote: Weaker trades let warm water spread eastward, reducing eastern upwelling.

03-la-nina.name: La Niña equatorial Pacific
03-la-nina.question: Compared with neutral conditions, what happens to eastern-Pacific upwelling?
03-la-nina.answerNote: Stronger trades pile warm water farther west and favor stronger eastern upwelling.

04-comparison.name: Compare ENSO-neutral, El Niño, and La Niña
04-comparison.question: Which state shifts the warm surface-water pool farthest east?
04-comparison.answerNote: El Niño shifts the warm pool eastward; La Niña pushes it farther west than neutral.
